question: Under NRS 278.353, a subdivider or developer who offers subdivided land for sale before the final map has been recorded with the county must:
choice_a: Wait until the map is recorded before accepting any deposit
choice_b: Provide the purchaser with the disclosures required by that statute before the sale is completed
choice_c: Obtain a special variance from the county recorder
choice_d: Notify only the State Engineer of the sale
explanation: NRS 278.353 imposes a disclosure obligation on sellers who offer subdivided property for sale before the final map is recorded, protecting purchasers who buy in advance of the map's completion.

question: On a Nevada subdivision final map, which party is required under NRS 278.374 to provide a certificate along with a report and guarantee of title?
choice_c: A title company, alongside the certificate of the owner of the land
explanation: NRS 278.374 requires the certificate of the owner of the land to be accompanied by a report and guarantee of title from a title company before a final subdivision map can be recorded.

question: NRS 278.375 requires which professional to certify a Nevada subdivision final map before it can be recorded?
explanation: NRS 278.375 requires the certificate of a professional land surveyor on the final map, verifying the survey underlying the subdivision.

question: For smaller divisions of land that do not require the full subdivision final-map process, Nevada law (NRS 278.461-278.469) provides an alternative, less burdensome procedure known as:
explanation: NRS 278.461 through 278.469 establish parcel map procedures as a reduced alternative to the full subdivision map process for qualifying land divisions.

question: Under NRS 119A.090, the person who coordinates timeshare sales on behalf of a developer and must hold a Nevada real estate broker's license under NRS 645 is known as the:
explanation: NRS 119A.090 defines a "project broker" as the individual who coordinates a developer's timeshare sales and who must be licensed as a real estate broker under chapter 645 of NRS.

question: Under NRS 119A.210, before a Nevada timeshare sales agent's license can be issued, the applicant must complete instruction covering ethics, timeshare law, and sales practices totaling:
explanation: NRS 119A.210 requires timeshare sales agent applicants to complete 14 hours of instruction in ethics, timeshare law, and sales practices, along with fingerprinting and a background check.

question: Under NRS 119A.220, a Nevada timeshare sales agent may be associated with:
choice_a: Up to three project brokers simultaneously
choice_b: Any broker licensed in any state
choice_c: No broker at all, provided the agent is bonded
choice_d: Only one project broker at a time
explanation: NRS 119A.220 limits a timeshare sales agent to association with a single project broker at a time, and requires the broker to notify the Real Estate Division within 10 days of the agent's termination.

question: Under NRS 119A.268, a licensee supervising a Nevada timeshare branch office must be a broker-salesperson with at least how much experience, and how many branch offices may one such supervisor oversee?
choice_a: 2 years of experience; only one branch office
choice_b: 1 year of experience; unlimited branch offices
choice_c: No minimum experience; up to 2 branch offices
choice_d: 5 years of experience; up to 3 branch offices
explanation: NRS 119A.268 requires branch office supervision by a broker-salesperson with at least 2 years of experience, and prohibits one supervisor from overseeing more than one branch office at a time.

question: Under NRS 119A.410, a purchaser of a Nevada timeshare interest has the statutory right to:
choice_a: Renegotiate the purchase price at any time before closing
choice_b: Cancel the contract of sale within a statutorily specified period after signing
choice_c: Transfer the timeshare to a third party without notifying the developer
choice_d: Demand a full refund at any time during the life of the timeshare plan
explanation: NRS 119A.410, titled "Right to cancel contract of sale," gives timeshare purchasers a statutory right of rescission during a defined period following execution of the purchase contract.

question: Nevada's water law, codified beginning at NRS 533.025, follows which doctrine of water rights?
choice_a: Riparian rights, under which water rights automatically attach to land bordering a water source
choice_b: Absolute ownership, under which landowners own all water beneath their land outright
choice_c: Prior appropriation, under which all water belongs to the public
choice_d: Correlative rights shared equally among all overlying landowners
explanation: NRS 533.025 declares that all water within Nevada's boundaries belongs to the public, reflecting Nevada's prior appropriation doctrine rather than a riparian rights system.

question: Under NRS 533.035, what is declared to be "the basis, the measure and the limit of the right to the use of water" in Nevada?
choice_a: Historical ownership of the underlying land
choice_b: The date the property was purchased
explanation: NRS 533.035 establishes beneficial use as the basis, measure, and limit of a Nevada water right; without beneficial use, no water right exists or continues.

question: Under NRS 533.040, a Nevada water right used for beneficial purposes is generally deemed to remain appurtenant to the place of use, but may be:
choice_a: Severed from the place of use and transferred to another place of use with State Engineer approval, without losing priority
choice_b: Sold separately from the underlying land without any state approval
choice_c: Automatically extinguished if the land is sold
choice_d: Converted into a riparian right upon transfer
explanation: NRS 533.040 allows a water right to be severed from its original place of use and transferred to a new place of use while retaining its priority date, subject to State Engineer approval of a change application under NRS 533.345.

question: Under NRS 534.180, a domestic well serving a single-family dwelling is exempt from Nevada's groundwater permitting requirements if it withdraws no more than:
explanation: NRS 534.180 exempts domestic wells withdrawing 2 acre-feet or less of water annually from the standard groundwater permitting process, though the State Engineer may still require registration in certain designated areas.

question: Under NRS 111.239, a deed restriction or covenant that prohibits or unreasonably restricts a homeowner's use of a solar energy system is:
choice_b: Enforceable if approved by the local planning commission
choice_d: Valid only for properties within a common-interest community
explanation: NRS 111.239 voids covenants, restrictions, or conditions in a deed or other instrument that prohibit or unreasonably restrict the use of a solar energy system, including restrictions that would reduce system efficiency by more than 10% without offering a comparable-cost alternative.

question: Under NRS 278.0208, a Nevada local government (city or county):
choice_a: May freely prohibit solar energy systems in single-family zoning districts
choice_b: May require solar systems to be removed after 20 years
choice_c: May charge an unlimited permit fee for solar installations
choice_d: Is prohibited from adopting an ordinance that prohibits or unreasonably restricts solar energy systems on residential property
explanation: NRS 278.0208 bars local governing bodies from adopting ordinances that prohibit or unreasonably restrict solar energy systems on residential property; NRS 278.02077 extends similar protections to wind energy systems.
